title: residency-proof-bundler-and-async-delivery-protocol
creator: Anika Patel
description: Introduce a residency-proof bundler service and an asynchronous delivery protocol to reliably package, sign, and deliver per-region residency attestations and retention manifests to customer endpoints and archival stores. This ticket covers: (1) bundling multiple residency/retention events into signed manifests with checksums, (2) a scheduler that sends manifests to configured destinations (webhook endpoints, S3/GCS buckets in-region) with exponential backoff and idempotency, and (3) console APIs and webhook contract changes to surface delivery state and re-delivery controls.
acceptance_criteria: Bundler service produces a signed manifest file (JSONL) containing one or more residency/retention events with SHA256 checksums and a top-level signature using the platform signing key.
Delivery scheduler honors per-customer delivery policies (immediate, batched-15m, daily) and per-region routing, and can target either webhooks or cloud buckets based on customer configuration.
Delivery protocol implements idempotency tokens and at-least-once semantics; duplicate manifests are detected and deduplicated by consumer using manifest_id and checksum.
Console exposes a delivery log with manifest-level status (queued, in-flight, delivered, failed), retry counts, and a manual re-deliver action for operators and customers with permission.
End-to-end e2e test coverage simulates transient failures, region failover, and legal-hold flags preventing deletion until release by a compliance admin.
Performance: bundler can create and sign manifests up to 10k events within 30s for large customers without blocking ingestion pipelines.
technical_notes: Manifest format: top-level manifest_id (UUIDv4), created_at ISO8601, region, retention_policy_id, events: array of event objects {event_id, type, timestamp, payload_pointer}, bundle_checksum: SHA256 of concatenated event checksums, signature: platform-signature (rsa-pss).

Storage: temporary staging in region-local object store (per-region S3/GCS) with lifecycle TTL. Final delivery includes signed HTTP POST (webhook) or putting object to customer bucket with server-side encryption and residency tags.

Scheduler: distributed leaderless scheduler built on job-queue (Kafka stream + consumer groups) with per-customer rate limits, jittered exponential backoff, and a bounded retry window configurable per-customer.
Idempotency: manifest_id + bundle_checksum used as the dedupe key. API must reject repeated deliveries older than 90 days unless explicitly reissued by operator.
Security: HSM/KMS used for signing; signature verification library published in SDKs. All delivery channels must support TLS1.2+ and webhook signing headers (X-RW-Signature).
Observability: tracing at manifest lifecycle boundaries, per-manifest metrics (size, event_count, latencies), and alerting for retry storms or per-customer backlog growth.

Backward compatibility: consumers expecting single-event webhooks will continue to receive single-event manifests; new batched manifest consumers must support JSONL parsing. We will version manifest with manifest_version=2.
Legal-hold: manifests marked with legal_hold=true are retained and flagged in the ledger; deletion APIs must be blocked until hold is cleared.
Privacy: payload pointers are signed references to encrypted audit objects; actual payloads remain in customer-scoped storage to prevent accidental cross-region leakage.
design_decisions: Use a signed manifest file for efficient verification at consumer side vs per-event signatures to reduce CPU overhead on high-volume customers.
Prefer object-store delivery for large batched manifests to avoid HTTP timeouts; add lightweight webhook notification containing manifest metadata for pull-based consumption.
Implement scheduler as eventually-consistent stream consumer to scale across regions; critical state (retry counts, next_attempt) stored in a small DynamoDB table for fast lookups.
Expose manual re-deliver and abort controls in Console instead of automated admin-only endpoints to reduce blast radius.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Deploy bundler + scheduler in us-west-2 and route 5% of compliance manifests for internal test orgs. Monitor delivery success and backlog metrics for 72h.
Phase 2 (limited): Enable per-customer batched delivery for customers in EMEA region with signed manifests and bucket delivery. Provide SDK verification helper in python/ts.
Phase 3 (general): Flip default for retention-manifests to batched delivery, document manifest v2 contract, and run a migration job for archived single-event consumers to support JSONL parsing.
Rollback plan: pause scheduler consumers for affected region; mark manifests as 'deferred' and fall back to existing single-event delivery mode while investigating.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Anika Patel: Initial ticket created after sync with Compliance and Console PMs. We agreed on signed manifest approach to reduce signature churn for high-volume customers.

2026-03-11 - Marco Ruiz: Spike complete. Implemented prototype that writes manifests to regional staging buckets and a consumer that posts to webhooks. Performance seems promising; signing is the CPU hotspot.
2026-03-12 - Laura Chen (Compliance PM): Reviewed acceptance criteria; added legal_hold and retention_policy_id requirements. Confirmed customers need manual re-deliver control via Console.
2026-03-13 - Marco Ruiz: Working on integrating KMS signing with HSM-backed keys. Open PR created and tests added. Next: implement idempotency checks and DynamoDB retry table.
